sentences.text:
Author: U. C. Dhyani
Bench: U. C. Dhyani

Hon'ble U. C. Dhyani, J.
Mr. S. K. Shandilya, Advocate present for the petitioner.

Mr. Raman Kumar Sah, Deputy Advocate General with Mr. Kuldeep Rawal, Brief Holder present for
the State.

By means of present criminal writ petition, the petitioner seeks to issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari quashing the impugned order dated 10.12.2014 passed by respondent no.2- Adjudicating Officer, Haridwar in case no.4 of 2014 under Section 51 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

The principal submission of learned counsel for the petitioner is that the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal has not been constituted in the State as yet and therefore, the petitioner cannot challenge the impugned order of the adjudicating Officer before the said Tribunal.
This Court was taken through the provisions of Sections 46(4), 68, 70, 71(6), 22 and 24 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
This Court was also taken through the provisions of the Rules 3.1.1.8, 3.1.1.9 and 3.1.1.12 of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011.
It is the statement of learned Deputy Advocate General that the establishment of Food Safety Appellate Tribunals at Dehradun and Haldwani is in the offing and shall become functional very soon.
No purpose will be served by keeping the present writ petition pending in view of the above statement of learned counsel for the State.

Criminal Writ Petition is thus disposed of by directing the petitioner to approach Food Safety Appellate Tribunal having jurisdiction within a month from the date the same becomes functional and till then the impugned order shall remain in abeyance.
(U. C. Dhyani, J.) Dated 24.03.2015 Rawat Samsher Gani vs State Of Uttarakhand & Others on 24 March, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174093229/
